eyebrow: Two quick ways to build one
code:
from qiskit import QuantumCircuit

qc = QuantumCircuit(2)        # 2 qubits, 0 classical bits
qc2 = QuantumCircuit(2, 2)    # 2 qubits, 2 classical bits
caption: Qubits are unnamed, addressed only by integer index — fine for small, throwaway circuits.

code:
from qiskit import QuantumRegister, ClassicalRegister, QuantumCircuit

qr = QuantumRegister(2, 'q')
cr = ClassicalRegister(2, 'c')
qc = QuantumCircuit(qr, cr)
caption: Functionally identical to QuantumCircuit(2, 2) — but named groups matter once a circuit combines, say, data qubits and ancilla qubits.

code:
qc = QuantumCircuit(2, 2)
qc.h(0)
qc.cx(0, 1)
qc.measure([0, 1], [0, 1])

print(qc.draw())    # text diagram, works anywhere
qc.draw('mpl')        # Matplotlib rendering
caption: The text diagram needs no extra dependencies and is the one you'll see most often while iterating quickly.
